newsitem.title: UK: Nissan will build 100,000 extra cars in UK.
newsitem.headline: Nissan will build 100,000 extra cars in UK.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co's 215 million stg investment in its plant at Sunderland, north east England to build a third new model is seen adding 100,000 cars of extra per annum capacity when production begins in 2000, its UK chief said on Tuesday.

Ian Gibson, UK managing director, told Reuters in an interview that production of a new model in the Pulsar range of mid-price cars, known as Almera in Europe, would add 100,000 extra vehicles. He added that the UK plant's productivity had won the day over the alternative suggestion to increase production in Japan and export more vehicles to Europe.
He said the UK division had to prove that it could produce the new model to "the same quality, and with similar efficiency and productivity levels as the plant in Japan."
Gibson added that the recent strong gains by sterling against the German mark was not perceived as a problem because the investment was a long term one, with production starting in 2000.
Nissan believed that damage to its UK exports due to sterling's gains could be offset by cost efficiencies in the long-term.
Nissan's European market share is around three percent.
